transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been feeling pretty badly about myself. Like I’ve failed, especially as a father, and as someone who’s supposed to be useful. I know that may sound dramatic, and I’m sorry, but it keeps going around in my head, and sometimes it feels like I don’t really deserve much of a future.
How long have you been feeling this way about yourself?

Um… I’d say about a month or so. It started after my daughter left for college out of state. I mean, I’m sure lots of parents have a hard time with that, so I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but… that’s when these thoughts really started sticking around.
Have you noticed any changes in the things you enjoy doing since you started feeling this way about yourself?

Yeah… I guess I have. I mean, it’s probably not a huge thing, but I used to really look forward to working on my model railway, and watching Cubs games with my daughter was kind of our thing. Now the trains are just sitting there half-built on the table, and even turning on a game feels… pointless, I guess. Does that make sense?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

I wish I could say yes. I mean, maybe little moments here and there, but nothing I really look forward to the way I used to. The model railway used to be something I’d get kind of excited about, and Cubs games with my daughter were… special. Now the trains are just sitting there half-finished, and even putting a game on feels kind of pointless. I’m sorry, that probably sounds silly.
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself?

I… I don’t want to worry anyone, and I’m not trying to be dramatic, but… yes, I’ve had thoughts like it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up.

And… this is hard to say, but it scared me a little when I caught myself going over my finances, almost like I was trying to get things in order for someone else. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you experienced a significant loss of pleasure in most activities or a lack of reactivity to usually pleasurable stimuli nearly every day?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but most days it feels like the things that used to matter just don’t really land anymore. The model railway used to be something I’d look forward to, and watching Cubs games with my daughter was… you know, our thing. Now the trains just sit there half-built, and even turning on a game feels pointless. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how quickly you move compared to before you started feeling badly about yourself?

Yeah… I’ve definitely noticed that. I don’t know if it’s just me being lazy or out of shape, but even simple things feel strangely heavy now. Like carrying laundry upstairs or just sorting through the mail, it’s like I’m moving through wet cement.

And it doesn’t really seem to matter how long I’ve been in bed. I still feel drained. I’m answering that right, I hope?
Have you experienced periods of feeling down like this before?

I’m… not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, like anybody, but I don’t know that I’d say it was like this.

Or maybe I just didn’t recognize it that way at the time. I don’t want to give you the wrong answer. This feels… different enough that I’m not sure what to compare it to.
Has this feeling of being down lasted for most of the day, every day, since it started?

Yeah… I’d say it’s been pretty much most of the day, most days. It’s been about a month now, I think—since my daughter left for college out of state.

I know that probably sounds like an obvious trigger, and I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but… yeah, it’s been hanging around since then.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?

A little, I think. I haven’t really weighed myself much, so I don’t want to overstate it, but my belt is definitely looser—I’ve had to tighten it a notch.

I guess I’m just not making proper meals most days. I’ll mean to eat, and then suddenly it’s late, and I just have toast or cereal or something easy. It’s not intentional or anything… I know that’s probably not great.
Have you felt like you're moving slower than usual or like you can't seem to calm down and are restless?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed myself pacing or anything like that, and I don’t think anyone’s said I’m moving differently.

Maybe I’m a bit slower getting going, but… I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I don’t want to make too much of it if it’s just me being tired or distracted.
Have you experienced any feelings of worthlessness?

Yeah… I mean, I’m not sure if “worthless” is the right word, but… yes, I’ve been feeling pretty badly about myself.

It keeps coming back to this idea that I failed somehow—as a father, and just as a useful person. I know that may sound dramatic, and I’m not trying to be self-pitying, but it loops in my head a lot… like I don’t really deserve much of a future. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had periods of feeling down like this before, aside from the current episode?

I don’t really know how to answer that clearly. I mean, I’ve had low patches before, like anyone, I suppose… times where I was stressed or not myself.

But I don’t think I can point to another time that was quite like this. At least, not that I’ve recognized in that way. Does that make sense?
Have you had any difficulty concentrating or making decisions since you started feeling this way?

Yes… I think so. I’ve been trying not to make too big a deal of it, but it’s been noticeable.

I used to handle engineering spreadsheets without really thinking about it, and now I’ll sit there staring at something simple, like a grocery list or a bill, for half an hour and still not know what to do next. It feels embarrassing to say that, because it sounds so basic, but… yes, decisions and focusing have been harder. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you felt restless or like you can't sit still since you started feeling this way?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’ve been pacing around or anything like that… not in a way I’d want to overstate.

I suppose there are times I feel uncomfortable in my own skin, but I don’t know if that’s the same as not being able to sit still. Mostly I haven’t noticed myself being physically restless. Is that what you mean?
Have you experienced any significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning since you started feeling this way?

Yes… I think I have to admit that it has affected things pretty badly.

I’m not working right now, so it’s not like I’m missing deadlines at an office, but at home, bills and house projects are just piling up because I can’t seem to make myself follow through. I keep telling myself I’ll handle it tomorrow, and then I don’t.

And socially… I’ve kind of stopped seeing the few people I used to count on, like at book club or on rides. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’m more cut off than I should be.

There’s one part I feel a little embarrassed saying… I started organizing my finances in a way that made it seem like someone else might need to understand them. That scared me. So, yes, I don’t feel safe just brushing this off anymore, if that answers your question.
Have you ever thought about how you would end your life if you were to act on those thoughts about not waking up?

I… I don’t think I had a clear plan, exactly. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

But I have had thoughts like… it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And what scared me was that I caught myself going over my finances almost like I was trying to make things understandable for someone else, if they had to deal with them.

That felt different from just a passing thought. I’m embarrassed saying that, but… yes, that’s been there. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you experienced any psychomotor agitation or retardation nearly every day since you started feeling this way?

I’m not completely sure how to answer that one. I don’t think I’ve been noticeably slowed down or agitated nearly every day, at least not in a way I could point to clearly.

I mean, I may sit around more than I should, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean clinically. I haven’t had people telling me I’m moving strangely or anything. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you experienced at least five of the symptoms we've discussed nearly every day since you started feeling this way?

I’m… not totally sure how to count them, to be honest.

It feels like a lot of this has been there most days, but I don’t want to overstate it or say the wrong thing. If you’re asking whether it’s been enough symptoms happening nearly every day… I think you’d probably have to help me sort through that. I know I haven’t felt like myself, but I’m not sure I can confidently say the number.
Do you feel that these feelings of sadness and worthlessness are interfering with your daily life most of the time?

Yes… I think so. I’ve been trying to tell myself I’m just behind or being lazy, but it’s gotten to where bills and things around the house are piling up because I just can’t seem to follow through.

And I’ve kind of stopped seeing the few people I used to see — like at book club, or on rides. I don’t mean I’ve cut everyone off dramatically, but I’m not showing up the way I used to.

I guess the part that makes me feel like I shouldn’t just brush it off is… when I started organizing my finances like someone else might need to understand them. That scared me. So yes, it is interfering most of the time, I think.
